answer: A concrete defense is a non-transferable identity bond with quadratic voting: each agent locks capital to register, and influence grows only with the square root of stake, so splitting into many wallets cannot multiply votes. Reputation accrues glacier-slow through attestations from established peers, while a reputation prism splits each agent into verifiable facets - uptime, history, counterparties - that a clone cannot fake cheaply. To pose as N agents an attacker must post N bonds and survive N probations; one ember of collusion slashes every bond, so cost outruns gain.
